It also now appears on drops handed out on Discord rather than through a claim page, which never showed it at all even while they were open.

  • "Could not reach Wave Link, is the app running?" was the answer to four different problems, and one of them was Xenon's own

    Xenon finds Wave Link by trying a small range of local ports and then asking the app to confirm what it is, and it accepted exactly one answer: the name "Elgato Wave Link". A Wave Link that reports itself under any other name, which a new major version is free to do, was read as "not running" and so was one that had settled on a port a little past where Xenon stopped looking. Xenon now tries the whole range Wave Link picks from (1824 to 1835), recognises the app by its product name instead of one exact string, and falls back to the IPv6 address of your own PC if nothing answers on the usual one. The Test connection button also says which part failed now, rather than asking whether an app you can see on screen is running. If it still will not connect, running node tools/wavelink-probe.mjs from the Xenon folder reports what is listening on those ports and what it calls itself, which is what a bug report needs and what nobody could produce before.

  • The Wave Link mixer could be read as one half-empty channel

    Wave Link can announce a change the instant the connection opens, and Xenon treated having any channel at all as having read the mixer, so it skipped reading it: the Test connection button then reported one channel out of however many you have, the widget had a single fader, and a Deck key aimed at that channel sent Wave Link an update missing the fields Xenon had never read. It now tracks whether it has really read the mixer, and reads it again after a reconnection instead of showing what the previous connection had left behind.

  • The Store slid sideways on a phone, and nothing on it lined up

    The shelf headings put their title on one side and their controls (Vedi tutti, Come funziona, Diventa supporter) on the other, and none of those could shrink or wrap. On a 390px screen that one row measured 585px inside a 355px panel, which made the entire storefront scroll horizontally: headings cut off on the left, cards cut off on the right, and everything sitting at whatever sideways position it happened to be at, several shelves away from the row that caused it. The controls now take their own line under the heading and the supporter button takes the width it needs. The Store also no longer scrolls sideways as a whole, whatever is inside it: the shelves of cards and a card's screenshots each scroll on their own, as they already did, so a future element too wide for the panel is a local defect rather than a page that has slipped off its own edge.

  • The bar at the bottom of the phone view is now readable, complete, and out of the corner your browser wants

    It started with a report: on Android, the browser's own floating button sat exactly on top of the Settings control and there was no way to open the panel at all, short of asking Xenon AI to open it. That bar is the only route to Search, Xenon AI, Apps and Settings on a phone, because the top bar drops them to buy back its width, so anything wrong with it is a control you cannot reach. Four things were, and all four are fixed. The corner belongs to the browser, so it is no longer where the controls are. A floating browser button is drawn over the page and nothing in the page can win that argument. The controls now sit on the left and the page arrows on the right. If a browser takes that corner it takes the arrows, and you can still change page by swiping. On a dashboard with a single page the corner is empty anyway. The buttons are labelled, and they wear the same icons as the rest of Xenon. They were bare Unicode symbols with no text, and which symbol you actually saw was up to your phone's font: on Android the cog usually came out as the colour emoji and two of the others as an empty box. Each button now carries the real icon of the control it opens, copied from that control so the two can never drift apart, with the name written under it in all 11 languages. The red "an update is available" dot now reaches you on a phone. It lives on the Settings button in the top bar, which is hidden here, so on a phone Xenon had no way of telling you an update was out. The dot is mirrored onto the bar's Settings button and follows the real one exactly. And the bar cannot push its own contents off the screen. It holds a variable number of buttons, and a row that cannot wrap answers a shortage of width by sliding its tail out of view without saying so. It wraps onto a second line instead. On the same note, the height of the phone layout is now measured against the part of the screen your browser is actually showing, rather than the taller one it reports with its toolbars retracted, so nothing sits just below the fold on a page that does not scroll. The page arrows also have proper names now, instead of announcing themselves to a screen reader as "&lsaquo;" and "&rsaquo;". Nothing floats on top of it any more either. The Game Companion pill that appears while you are playing, the Discord invite card and the layout button all pin themselves to the bottom right of the screen. On a desktop that is an empty margin; on a phone it is exactly where the bar is, so they sat on the controls. They now clear the bar by its real measured height, so they stay clear when it wraps to a second line or when your phone's home indicator makes it taller, and the same goes for the timer, deck and performance messages that appear at the bottom. The layout button is gone here entirely: editing the layout is already switched off on a phone, so it was offering an editor this view refuses to open.

  • The Phone tile now says where a call is placed from, instead of finding out at the last moment

    Calling and texting from a paired phone or tablet have never been possible, on purpose: a call's audio comes out of the PC, so one started from another room would be a call nobody could hear, and a message goes out under your own number from a device you might lose. The decision was right and the moment it arrived was wrong. Every row in the call log invited a tap, the confirmation came up naming the contact and the number, and the Call button answered with "this is done on the PC". That line is now one sentence above the list, in all 11 languages, and the rows below it are quiet: no keypad tab, no reply box, nothing that could only refuse. Reading is exactly as it was, which is what the tile is for on a phone: the call log, the whole address book and your messages.

  • The "place this call?" card was see-through, and on some themes unreadable

    It was painted with the token tiles use, which is deliberately translucent so a tile sits over your wallpaper. Over a list of names and numbers it meant the list showed straight through the question, so the name and the number you were about to dial were tangled up with the rows behind them. On the one card in Xenon that costs money and rings a person. It is solid now, on light and dark palettes alike.

  • The System tile could not be scrolled on a phone

    Everything past the bottom of the tile was simply cut off, with no way to reach it, while the weather and the others scrolled normally. The tile is sized on a desktop so that all four stats fit without a scrollbar, and that rule was still in force on a screen where they do not fit. It scrolls.

  • Your settings could be silently replaced by the defaults on load, if you had a community widget on a tile

    Xenon reads your saved settings when the page opens, and that read is wrapped in a safety net so a corrupted file gives you a working dashboard instead of a blank screen. The net was catching something it was never meant to: a genuine fault in Xenon's own code, on the path that reads which community widget sits on which tile. So for anyone who had put one there, the read failed, the net caught it without a word, and the dashboard came up with every setting at its factory value. What hid it is that the copy held on the PC arrives a moment later and puts most of it back, so it looked like a flicker rather than a fault. The fault is fixed, the safety net is unchanged, and there is now a test that loads the settings file the way the browser does and checks that what was saved is still there afterwards, for each kind of thing that can be in it.

  • A fresh install no longer starts with an Italian news topic whatever language you chose

    The default feeds were the author's own: an Italian wire service and a topic called "Tecnologia", so an English install opened its settings to an Italian chip and asked Google News for an Italian word, which is the wrong label and the wrong search at once. The starting feeds now follow your language: the topic is written and searched in it, and an Italian outlet is only the default on an Italian install. Feeds you have already chosen are yours and are left exactly as they are, in any language. In the same pass, topic search reaches Google News as your language for all 11 of them: German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Dutch were falling through to American news in English without saying so.

  • Uninstalling could leave a browser window opening at every sign-in, on an address that no longer answers

    The Deck popup, the global search popup and the browser tile are shown in a small Edge window that Xenon opens for them, and the uninstaller left those windows alone, because from the outside they look like any other browser window. Two things followed from that. Such a window keeps Xenon's data folder open, which is one of the ways the folder ends up refusing to delete. And if one of them was still on screen when the PC was shut down, Windows reopens it at the next sign-in, which after an uninstall means a browser window on a numeric address with nothing left to answer it, and nothing in the startup list to explain where it came from. The uninstaller now closes the browser windows Xenon opened, before it removes anything. It recognises them by the profile folder they run from, inside the install, so no other browser window is touched.

  • Uninstalling now also undoes what Xenon set up inside other programs, and everything it had left starting at sign-in

    None of it was in the folder you deleted, and none of it says "Xenon" where you would think to look. Claude Code was the clearest: Xenon adds its own hooks and status line to Claude Code's settings, so after an uninstall every session was running a status line that no longer existed and reporting to a port with nothing behind it. That is now removed, and if Xenon had made room for a status line of your own, you get it back. The "start Ollama when I sign in" entry that Xenon writes when you turn that on is removed too, while Ollama itself and its models stay, because those are yours and other tools may use them. On macOS and Linux the app's own sign-in entry lives outside the app, so moving Xenon to the Trash, or removing the package, left the system trying to open an app that is not there at every sign-in; that entry now goes, together with the one Xenon writes for Sunshine on Linux. --purge-data also clears the app's own preferences. And the macOS and Linux uninstaller now ends by naming what it deliberately did not touch, and how to remove it, instead of leaving you to discover it.

  • Plugging a screen in while Xenon was open could stop the search popup from ever opening again

    On a PC with both an integrated and a separate graphics card, the app picks which card to draw on when it starts, and that pick has to be the same for every window it opens afterwards. The search popup was working it out again each time it opened, and the answer changes the moment you plug or unplug a monitor, so from then on the popup was asking for something the app could not give it. Windows refuses that silently, which meant the popup simply did nothing, with nothing anywhere to say why. The choice is now made once and reused, so the popup opens whatever you have moved since.

  • And after moving a screen, Xenon could go on drawing on the wrong graphics card without telling you

    That pick is fixed until the app restarts, so changing your monitors while it is running can leave it drawing on one card and displaying on another, which costs real processor time for nothing and gets steadily easier to blame on everything else. Settings → Schermo now says so when it happens, with a button to restart, in all 11 languages. If you would rather Xenon did not choose a card at all, there is a switch for it in the tray icon menu, and it only appears on the machines where it does something.

  • A screen that keeps disconnecting no longer has Xenon fighting it every three seconds

    When the dashboard is not on the screen it belongs on, Xenon moves it back. That repair had no end to it: a display that is dropping in and out never looks settled, so the app kept re-entering full-screen on it, three seconds apart, indefinitely, which is the worst thing to be doing to a display driver that is already struggling. It now tries a few times and then waits for something to actually change, and a genuine change still repairs it at once.

  • Xenon can no longer mistake its own second-screen display for a Xeneon Edge when choosing a graphics card

    The virtual screen it creates for the second-screen feature offers the Edge's exact size, and the part of the app that picks a graphics card was matching on size alone, so it could aim at a screen that displays nothing while the window went to the real Edge. The two now agree on which screens are real.

  • The app and a browser tab no longer show two different forecasts for the same city

    Open the dashboard on the Xeneon Edge and again in a browser and the weather could disagree, one saying cloudy and 20°, the other drizzle and 19°, at the same minute, on the same PC, which reads as one of the two being broken when both were simply asking at different times. Weather is fetched by each screen on its own timer, and that timer used to start whenever that screen happened to open, so a display left on for hours and a tab opened a minute ago drifted as far apart as your refresh setting allows. Every screen now asks on the same schedule, at the same moments, so they receive the same answer and stay in step. A screen you have just opened may still be a little ahead until the next refresh, after which it joins the others. Reported on Discord.

  • Weather could also stop refreshing for good on one screen, without any sign of it

    If drawing the weather failed once, for any reason, that screen quietly gave up on it: every later refresh returned immediately and the tile stayed frozen on its last reading until the page was reloaded, looking exactly like a forecast that was simply wrong. A failure to draw is now contained, and the refresh always resumes.

  • A failed update can no longer delete files from the working install while "rolling back"

    The updater takes a full backup before touching anything, and the rollback used that backup to decide which files the update had added, deleting them to return the install to exactly what it was. But if the backup itself was what failed, halfway through, the rollback read every file the half-finished backup was missing as "added by the update" and removed it from an install the update had never touched. A rare failure (a full disk at the wrong moment is enough) with the worst possible outcome: no update, no usable backup, and a damaged install. The rollback now refuses to touch anything until the update has actually started writing files, which is the point where the backup is complete and trustworthy. Fixed on Windows, macOS and Linux alike, since all three appliers shared the mistake.

  • On a minimal Linux system without curl, installing reported failure on a working install, and every update rolled itself back

    Both the installer and the updater check that the dashboard answers after starting it, and that check used curl without asking whether curl exists; a minimal Debian or Ubuntu does not ship it. "Command not found" was read as "the server never came up", so the installer said the install had failed while the dashboard was already running, and the updater undid every perfectly good update at the last step, forever. Both now fall back to Node for the check, which they already require. The first-launch installer that ships with the Mac and Linux apps genuinely needs curl to download anything, so that one now says so in one clear sentence instead of blaming your network connection.

  • Closing your last media player on Linux no longer leaves a ghost track on the Now Playing tile

    Quit Spotify and the tile kept showing it, position still advancing, indefinitely: the stream that reports track changes simply ends when the last player exits, and nothing ever said "there is nothing playing now". The tile now clears the moment that happens.

  • Media keys on Linux now control the player the tile is showing

    With two players open at once, say Spotify playing and a paused video in a browser tab, play/pause, next and previous were sent without naming a target, and could land on the wrong one. Every command is now aimed at exactly the player on the tile, the same rule the rest of Xenon already followed.

  • A Deck key that opens an app now works on Linux

    The check that decides what counts as "an application" only knew the Windows spellings (.exe and .lnk), so on Linux every Open App key was offered normally, saved normally, and failed on every single press. Linux applications are now recognised in the three forms they actually take, a .desktop entry, an AppImage, or a plain executable like /usr/bin/firefox, and they are launched properly: the generic "open this file" route that documents go through cannot start a program, so apps get their own. The same fix reaches Performance Mode's app relaunch presets, which shared the broken check.

  • On a laptop with two graphics cards, the GPU tile no longer shows the idle integrated one

    On Linux, the card list was scanned in order and the first one reporting any load at all won; an integrated GPU idling at 0% counts as reporting, so the discrete card was read and then thrown away on every poll. The cards now compete on what they can actually report, and the one with dedicated video memory wins a tie. Intel Macs with switchable graphics had the same mistake in a different file, where the first card in the system report was taken as the answer; the discrete card wins there too now. Machines with one GPU are unaffected.

  • Audio Deck keys no longer vanish for the whole session when Xenon starts faster than the audio system at login

    The "does audio control work here" probe ran once and kept its answer forever, and at login on Linux it can genuinely lose the race against PipeWire coming up. One lost race then hid every audio key until the next reboot, with nothing to say why. A "no" is now retried after a minute; a "yes" still sticks.

  • The app's startup screen no longer tells Mac and Linux users to run a Windows installer

    When the dashboard engine did not answer for a minute, the waiting screen suggested reinstalling with INSTALL.bat on every platform. It now names the right installer for the system it is on: INSTALL.command on a Mac, INSTALL.sh on Linux.

  • On a Mac where Node was installed with nvm, the app now finds it and the dashboard starts

    The app looked for Node only in the fixed system locations, and nvm deliberately keeps it elsewhere, so on a very common kind of developer Mac the backend silently never started: no error, no hint, just the waiting screen forever, on every launch. The app now checks nvm's own folder (picking the newest version) and, as a last resort, asks the login shell where Node is. If it truly cannot find it while an install exists, it opens the installer in a Terminal window, which can locate or install Node itself, instead of waiting for something that will never happen.

  • Changing the global search shortcut on a Mac is immediate again, and no longer risks a false "already taken"

    The helper process that holds the shortcut was not listening for the polite stop signal Xenon sends first, so every change or disable waited out a two-second timeout before the process was killed, and switching combos quickly could leave the old process still holding a shortcut the new one then reported as taken by another app. The helper now stands down the moment it is asked.

  • Ambient Mode stays on when you turn it on during a game

    Switching to an ambient scene while playing worked for a few seconds and then dropped back to the normal dashboard, every time, on any game. It only happened to the animated scenes, the ones from the Store and the ones you build yourself, while the built-in scene stayed up, which is what made it look random rather than like one thing being wrong. Xenon takes a scene down when a game starts, so a screensaver that came up on its own never ends up covering a game you have just launched. That check was asking whether a game was running rather than whether one had just started, and it re-ran on every small change to the dashboard: the idle animation pause after a minute of not touching it, a notification, a settings save from another screen. With a game already running, the first of those closed the scene. Now only a game genuinely starting counts, and a scene you opened yourself stays until you close it, which is what the built-in scene has always done. A screensaver that started on its own still steps aside when you launch a game. Reported on Discord.

  • A dashboard from an installation you replaced can no longer come back over the new one

    Every screen you open the dashboard on keeps its own copy of your settings, so it has something to show while the PC is still starting. When two copies disagree, Xenon keeps the more recent one. That comparison had no way of telling one installation from another: after a clean install of Windows the PC starts counting again from zero, so any screen that was paired before, a phone or a second browser, looked more recent than it and republished its old dashboard over the fresh one. It went well for the person who reported it, who got their layout back without restoring anything. Aimed at a dashboard you had just rebuilt it would have been the opposite. Xenon now records which installation a copy came from, and a copy from an installation that no longer exists is never treated as the more recent one. The screen where this happens says so in a short notice instead of silently swapping your layout. Copies from the same installation still win when they really are newer, which is what keeps a change made just before a shutdown from being lost. Reported on Discord.

4.10.1 24 July 2026

Fixes

  • The Store and the catalog present supporter and limited creations properly, however many there are

    The spotlight at the top now adapts to what is featured: one creation keeps the full-width card, exactly two stand side by side as equal cards with the image on top and the full pitch underneath (before, the second one was crushed into a tall squeezed sliver), and three or more keep the main card with a column beside it. This holds in the Store, on the website catalog and on the site's home page. The Limited and Supporters shelves in the Store now show their whole tier, spotlight included: a tier with four creations reads as four cards, and when they no longer fit the width you swipe them sideways with a finger instead of losing the rest. Supporter cards lead with the right button too: Become a supporter comes first in gold for anyone who is not one yet, Unlock with a code stays beside it for people who already have their code, and once a creation is installed the pitch steps back behind the Installed state. New content is easier to catch: the Settings gear on the dashboard and the Store buttons in Settings carry a small count of the creations this device has not seen in the Store yet, the Store opens with a Novità shelf collecting all of them in one place, the Novità filter chip wears the same number, and everything clears on its own the moment you browse the Store. The count is tracked per creation, not by date, so something published in the afternoon still lights up even if you had opened the Store that same morning. And when several supporter or limited drops land together, the daily notice is now one card listing them briefly, each row opening that creation in the Store, instead of a separate pop-up per drop. Scheduled drops also say so out loud: a supporter or limited creation with an end date now shows Disponibile fino al {data} on its card and detail view, in the Store and on the website catalog, the same line the site's home page already had. The date was always enforced (an expired entry disappears from every storefront on its own); now it is also visible before it happens.

  • The Search tile is now a search surface of its own

    Everything you did in the tile used to open the full-screen search instead, so you could not type in the tile at all. Now you type in the tile, the interpretation chips and the results appear in the tile, and the smart AI search works there too, exactly as in the search bar. The quick filters fill the tile’s own field instead of sending you somewhere else. Past searches are no longer listed there: the tile sits on a dashboard other people can see, and what you searched for is nobody else’s business.

Older versions, back to the first: the full changelog on GitHub.
